mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to equity valuation multiples, with lower rates reducing the discount rate applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL > 265) signals elevated inflation, triggering monetary tightening that compresses equity valuation multiples and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 265), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5%) and Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL > 265) co-occur, the combination signals an inflationary policy tightening cycle that compresses equity valuation multiples and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5% AND CPIAUCSL > 265) fails to produce negative returns in more than 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
